I've done this a couple times and thought I'd share it with everyone.

Blu-rays from Canada, Mexico, and Japan have the same region code as the US, so any discs from these locations will work in a standard US Blu-ray player. No need to buy a more expensive 'region-free' or 'all-region' player.

Amazon.ca is the Canadian Amazon site, and you can often find good deals there. I will use, for an example, this Lord of the Rings Blu-ray set. $59.99 USD with free shipping on the US Amazon site. If you hop over to Amazon.ca, however, you'll see that it costs $40.99 CDN, which equates to $32.37 USD. Shipping is not free for international shipping, but for this item it will cost about $9 USD. In the end you will get the Lord of the Rings Blu-ray set for about $42 USD, as apposed to $59.99. You can also check the Mexican and Japanese Amazon sites, but I find they're usually not worth it (the set costs ~$80 USD on both of these sites before shipping).

What's more, you still get the same Amazon service. My Blu-ray set I bought happened to have a bad Return of the King disc and I was able to send it back for a refund, no problem. Shipping takes longer, but I'll gladly wait a few more days to receive an item to save $18 just about any day of the week.

Also, on a slightly related note, it's worth knowing Blu-ray region codes. I'm a big Terry Gilliam fan and was eagerly awaiting the release of The Zero Theorem. The Blu-ray was released in the UK (which is Region B and will not usually have discs which will work in the US) before we even had a theatrical release over here in the states, and the disc was encoded to work in region A, B, and C. I bought the movie on Amazon.co.uk and watched it with my friends before it was even released theatrically over here. Definitely keep an eye out for all international releases of much awaited films. Every once in a while you'll get lucky and will be able to find one that will work in your player.

TL;DR: Canadian Blu-rays can save you mucho bucks.
